body:
FROM THE P5 SUPPRESSION LENS, 2026-08-19. Three silent failures in one function; T191 covers the
lift half separately.

1. `.find` PICKS ONE BINDING AND SNAPSHOT ORDER DECIDES WHICH. Several bindings survive at one entity
   by design — readRegistrations takes the latest per (registration entity, lens name) and
   readRegistrationVersions returns every survivor. If a lens has a v1 and a v2, striking v1 leaves
   v2 latest and THE LENS KEEPS SERVING while the curse reports done.

2. THE MATCH IS ON THE HYPERSCHEMA ENTITY, NOT THE LENS — H6's shape, in the bytes. Under §21.7
   coexistence two readings share one entity, so cursing one lens can strike a SIBLING reading's
   binding while the cursed lens keeps serving. Exactly the wrong lens retired.

3. `binding === undefined` RETURNS SUCCESS HAVING STRUCK NOTHING. Registration.entity is optional, so
   a manually-registered lens has none and both comparisons are false. The docstring one line above
   promises "the lens leaves the surface". H7.

WHY THE RAIL CANNOT SEE ANY OF IT: curse-durable.test.ts uses two distinct programs (Plant, Sprout),
each with one entity and one version — the corpus in which the entity-match and the lens-match
COINCIDE. That is H10 ("two derivations coincide"), and it is why a green rail proves nothing here.

FIX SHAPE: collect ALL live bindings whose lens name is the living name, strike each, then ASSERT the
lens no longer serves and REFUSE if it does. A curse that cannot prove the lens left must not report
that it did.
title: curseChannelLaw strikes one binding, matched by entity rather than lens, and can report success having struck nothing
